scenes.goal: find out who wrote the letter signed with her dead father's name
scenes.opposition: Crane will not let the warden read his ledger and rows away

turningPoint.description: Captain Thorne shows Elspeth a letter about the Margery's cargo signed with her father's name
turningPoint.evidence: The letter is signed with your father's name.

evidence.goal: "I would like to know who wrote this letter."
evidence.opposition: "Not today, Captain." He pushed off from the landing without another word
evidence.outcome: "Then we go to Stavely," Jonas said.

scenes.goal: learn in Stavely who posted the letter
scenes.opposition: the boy who carried the letter does not know who paid him, and the warden suspects their father

turningPoint.description: Thorne tells them the Margery carried the parish gold, and that Crane is dying
turningPoint.evidence: She was carrying a strongbox with the Wenlow parish money in it, sixty pounds in gold, sent to the bank at Stavely for safekeeping.

evidence.goal: "Then you'll want to know that the warden came in on horseback this afternoon.
evidence.opposition: "And you think my father stole it," Elspeth said.
evidence.outcome: If he knows anything, he will not know it for long.

scenes.goal: get the truth from Crane before he dies
scenes.opposition: Crane's ten years of silence and his failing breath

turningPoint.description: Crane confesses he wrote the letter and gives Elspeth the ledger and the key to the strongbox
turningPoint.evidence: He reached under his pillow with a shaking hand and pressed the ledger and a small iron key into her hands.

evidence.opposition: "I was a coward for ten years, Elspeth. I am too tired to be one now."
evidence.outcome: "The strongbox is under the third flagstone of the abbey chapel on Gorse Hill," Crane said.

scenes.goal: dig up the strongbox from under the abbey chapel floor
scenes.opposition: the warden appears and demands the box

turningPoint.description: Elspeth refuses to hand the strongbox to Thorne and carries it back to Wenlow herself
turningPoint.evidence: "We are taking it back to Wenlow ourselves," said Elspeth.

evidence.goal: Elspeth counted the flagstones from the chapel door.
evidence.opposition: "Now you give that box to me."
evidence.outcome: Elspeth carried the strongbox down the hill herself, though it bruised her arms.

scenes.opposition: Alderman Pask and the men on the parish council who sank the Margery

turningPoint.description: Elspeth gives the ledger to the warden and names Alderman Pask
turningPoint.evidence: She gave the ledger to Captain Thorne.

evidence.opposition: "There are three names in it," Elspeth said. "One of them is Alderman Pask."
